question: By selling an article at (2)/(5) of its actual selling price, Nirbhay incurs a loss of 26%. If he sells it at 84% of its actual selling price, then the profit percentage is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the actual selling price be SP and cost price be CP.

Selling at 2/5 of SP means 0.4 SP, which results in a 26% loss.

0.4 SP = 0.74 CP ⇒ SP = 1.85 CP

New Selling Price = 0.84 SP = 0.84 × 1.85 CP = 1.554 CP

Profit % = (1.554 − 1) × 100 = 55.4%

**∴ The correct answer is 55.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loss = 26% when SP₁ = 2/5 × Actual SP

New Selling Price SP₂ = 84% × Actual SP

 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 SP₁
 0.4 SP
 (74% CP)

 Cost Price
 1.0 CP
 (100% CP)
 
 SP₂
 0.84 SP
 (155.4% CP)

 Actual SP
 1.0 SP
 (185% CP)
 
 
 

 ← 26% Loss
 
 

 55.4% Profit →

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Actual SP be 100x.

⇒ SP₁ = (2/5) × 100x = 40x

⇒ Since selling at 40x incurs a 26% loss, the Cost Price (CP) will be calculated as:

⇒ CP × (100 − 26)% = 40x

⇒ CP × 0.74 = 40x

⇒ CP = 40x / 0.74 = 4000x / 74 = 2000x / 37

⇒ Now, the new selling price SP₂ = 84% of Actual SP = 84x

⇒ Profit = SP₂ − CP = 84x − (2000x / 37)

⇒ Profit = (3108x − 2000x) / 37 = 1108x / 37

⇒ Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = [(1108x / 37) / (2000x / 37)] × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1108 / 2000) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 1108 / 20 = 55.4%

**∴ The correct answer is 55.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit & Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss / CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) / 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is calculated as (a + b − ab / 100)%.
